message.content:
Here are a few popular sushi spots you might want to try in Tokyo:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|-------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (and other branches) | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; Michelin‑starred experience; very limited seating and high price. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | Intimate setting, top‑tier nigiri, often considered one of the best in the world. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | Elegant atmosphere, meticulous preparation, Michelin‑starred. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Famous for fresh fish and long lines; great value for the quality. |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations | Casual, open‑air counter, good for a quick bite or late‑night craving. |
| **Umegaoka Sushino Midori** | Shibuya | Known for affordable, high‑quality sushi; popular among locals and tourists alike. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic ambiance, excellent omakase options, well‑known for consistency. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Roppongi | Small, intimate, highly regarded for its seasonal selection. |

If you’re planning a visit, it’s wise to make reservations ahead of time—especially for the Michelin‑starred places—and keep in mind that many of them have strict dress codes and may require a deposit. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
